question.text: After establishing the government of Ankara, this man led the War of Turkish Independence and became the first president of the Republic of Turkey.
question.clue: He captured Mus while defeating Russian forces in the Caucasus, and this leader won the battle of Sakarya over the Greeks, earning the Treaty of Lausanne, which annulled the earlier and harsher Treaty of Sevres.

swap.text: Celtic culture spread as far as this country after the ancient Galatians settled down. This country warred with Greece after World War I under its leader, Mustafa Kemal Ataturk.
swap.clue: Herodotus, author of the Histories, was native of this modern-day country, as he was born in Halicarnassus.

question.text: This sultan was surprised by Wallachian troops during the Night Attack at Targoviste [ter-GOH-vish-te], after which Vlad impaled 20,000 Turks. This sultan also invaded Serbia and captured Constantinople.
question.answerHtml: Mehmed II [accept Mehmed the Conqueror; accept “Mehmet” in place of “Mehmed”]
question.clue: This ruler established a millet led by Gennadius II, who received authority over all Orthodox Christians in his empire.

swap.text: Ottoman authorities exterminated these people during World War One, often by marching them into the Syrian desert. These Christian people were considered of suspect loyalty by the Ottomans.
swap.clue: Thanks to Gregory the Illuminator, these people had the world's first official Christian state starting in 301.

question.leadin: These troops were divided into battalions called ortas, which were then led by corbaci ["chor-ba-jee"].
question.text: Name this elite corps of rifle-wielding soldiers, which was established by Murad I. These troops were partially recruited by the devshirme ["dev-shir-muh"] system.
question.answerHtml: Janissaries [“jan-ih-sair-ees”] [or word forms, such as the Janissary Corps; or Yeniceri]
question.clue: In a coronation ceremony for a monarch sometimes called "The Sot" or "The Drunkard", this group refused to march to the Topkapi Palace until bribed, and they originally served as a bodyguard for Orkhan.

swap.leadin: It is known as the first modern genocide.
swap.text: Name this holocaust that took place in the Ottoman Empire, which targeted a namesake group of Middle Eastern Christians.
swap.answerHtml: Armenian Genocide [or Armenian Massacre or Armenian Holocaust or The Great Calamity or The Great Crime or Ermeni Soykinmi or Mec Egert]
swap.clue: Comments about this event in the documentary Screamers presaged the trial for "insulting" a nationality and the murder of Hrant Dink.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about the military personnel of Australia.
question.text: This World War I battle, a disaster planned by Winston Churchill, was fought largely by the ANZAC corps of Australians and New Zealanders. Mustafa Kemal gained fame defending Turkey here.
question.clue: This World War I battle, also known as the Dardanelles Campaign, that ended in an Ottoman victory over ANZAC forces.

swap.text: One contention in the history wars was the celebration of ANZAC [ANN-zack] day, which honors the participants in this failed 1915-16 campaign attacking a peninsula in modern-day Turkey.
swap.clue: Charles Monro replaced Ian Hamilton as head of one side's troops during it.

question.text: The genocide was carried out by the Committee of Union and Progress under three de facto leaders with this title. Talaat and Ahmed Cemal ("keh-mal"), who both had this title, were assassinated for their role in the genocide during Operation Nemesis.
question.answerHtml: Pasha [accept Three Pashas or İsmail Enver Pasha or Mehmed Talaat Pasha or Ahmed Cemal Pasha or Djemal Pasha]
question.clue: The genocide was carried out by the Committee of Union and Progress under three de facto leaders with this title. Talaat and Ahmed Cemal ("keh-mal"), who both had this title, were assassinated for their role in the genocide during Operation Nemesis.

swap.text: In 1699, this treaty ended the war between the Ottomans and the Holy League, during which Eugene of Savoy won the Battle of Zenta. It forced the Ottomans to give up Transylvania to Austria.
swap.clue: Its Russian portion was supplemented in the following year by a treaty which transferred Azov, and it exempted an area defined by the Tisza, Mures, and Danube rivers, the Banat of Temesvar, from one provision.

question.text: This son of Selim the Grim conquered Hungary after the Battle of Mohacs and defeated the Safavids. He was nicknamed "the Lawgiver" for his reforms.
question.answerHtml: Suleiman I [or Suleiman the Magnificent; or Sulayman al-Qanuni] [10] This sultan’s reign saw reforms known as the Tanzimat, such as the dissolution of the Janissaries in the Auspicious Incident and the adoption of more European-style dress and customs by the aristocracy. ANSWER: Mahmud II
question.clue: This ruler expelled the Knights Hospitalers from Rhodes after conquering Belgrade, although the same group would defeat him at Malta later on.

swap.leadin: This battle is considered to be the turning point in the Ottoman conquest of Europe.
swap.text: Name this 1529 clash that marked the farthest reach of Ottoman troops into the west. At this battle, Niklas Graf Salm defended a Habsburg city from siege.

question.leadin: A "protocol" named for this city called for Israel to invade Egypt, after which Britain and France would issue disingenuous statements that they had to seize the Suez Canal to maintain its neutrality.
question.text: Name this French city. A treaty named for this city confirmed an armistice signed in Moudros Harbor and divided a country into Italian, French, British, and Greek zones of occupation.

swap.leadin: After the Alhambra Decree, a ruler with this name resettled Sephardic Jews into his empire's city of Salonica.
swap.text: Give this name shared by two Ottoman Sultans, the first of which was captured at the Battle of Ankara.
swap.clue: Another ruler of this name allegedly committed suicide by banging his head against some bars after being forced to live in a cage.

question.leadin: This initiative resulted in the creation of provincial courts as part of the Vilayet Law, replacing the eyalet system.
question.text: Name this initiative that included the decriminalization of homosexuality and a "reform edict" granting religious freedom to all. This mid-19th century initiative's goals were laid out in the "Supreme Edict of the Rosehouse."
question.clue: The Rescript of the Rose Chamber promised the end of tax farming during this period, during which changes in the millet system attempted to curb nationalism among religious minorities.

swap.leadin: This period saw the creation of the Arazi Kanunnamesi land code and efforts at promoting religious equality through the Imperial Reform Edict.
swap.text: Name this period begun by the Rescript of the Rose Chamber.
swap.clue: This period of reform in the Ottoman Empire begun by the Rescript of the Rose Chamber. This period included the abolition of the millet system and the elimination of tax farming.

question.text: After being irked by the Treaty of Sevres, Ataturk pushed for the signing of this 1923 treaty, which offered more concessions to Turkey and established the nation's modern borders.
question.clue: An earlier treaty signed at the same location was also called the Treaty of Ouchy, and ended the Italo-Turkish War in 1912.

swap.leadin: At the end of this novel, Gabriel Bagradian is killed while standing over his son's grave, but not before he manages to get his fellow townsmen on a ship.
swap.text: Identify this novel set during the Armenian genocide, in which the Turks attempt to seize the title mountain.
swap.answerHtml: The Forty Days of Musa Dagh [or Die vierzig Tage des Musa Dagh]
swap.answer: The Forty Days of Musa Dagh

question.text: As with the various denominations of Christians in the empire, this system granted the Ottoman Jewish community much autonomy over their internal affairs.
question.clue: This system, which allowed religious minorities to live independently of Islamic law, was abolished by the Tanzimat reforms in an attempt to reduce nationalist tendencies.

swap.text: The Ottoman forces at Nicopolis were led by this sultan, who later died while imprisoned by Tamerlane.
swap.clue: This man's reign was followed by a twelve year power struggle known as the Interregnum before the confirmation of Mehmet I as sultan.
